title: Colour-equivalent approximations are marked operadic weak equivalences
statement:
Use symmetric infinity operads, inert markings and the categorical-pattern model category $\mathsf M$ of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition], and quasicategories and inner/cocartesian fibrations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be a small symmetric infinity operad. A pointed map is active if only its basepoint maps to the basepoint.

Call a categorical fibration $g:D\to P$ an approximation when (i) for every $d$ over $\langle n\rangle$ and every colour projection $\rho_i$ there is a locally $pg$-cocartesian edge $d\to d_i$ over $\rho_i$ whose image in $P$ is inert, and (ii) every active edge $z\to g(d)$ in $P$ admits a $g$-cartesian lift with target $d$. Locally cocartesian means cocartesian in the pullback over the specified edge. A coherent functor $f:C\to P$ is an approximation if, over $P$, it factors as a categorical equivalence followed by such a categorical fibration. Mark an edge of $C$ exactly when its image in $P$ is inert, and write $C^{\mathrm{in}/P}$ for this marked object.

If $f:C\to P$ is an approximation and its colour-fibre functor $C\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}\{\langle1\rangle\}\to P_{\langle1\rangle}$ is an equivalence, then the marked map
$$f:C^{\mathrm{in}/P}\longrightarrow P^{\mathrm{in}}$$
is a weak equivalence in $\mathsf M$. This assertion includes arbitrary coherent approximations, without a categorical-fibration hypothesis on $f$ itself.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definitions 2.3.3.6 and 2.3.3.25, Lemma 2.3.3.10 (approximations are weak approximations) and Theorem 2.3.3.23(1) together with the weak-equivalence test in Proposition 2.1.4.6; also the consequence recorded in Remark 2.3.3.27 after Theorem 2.3.3.26. The unary equivalence hypothesis of the preceding theorem is retained when using Remark 2.3.3.27. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: Choose a witness $f=ge$ to the approximation hypothesis, with $e:C\to D$ a categorical equivalence and $g:D\to P$ a categorical-fibration approximation. We will verify the weak-approximation conditions of [lem-coef-symmetric-weak-approximation-algebras] for this same $g$. Its local colour-projection lifts are already supplied by the hypothesis. Fix $d\in D$ and an arbitrary edge $\alpha:x\to g(d)$. By [lem-coef-symmetric-inert-active-orthogonality] choose a coherent factorization $x\xrightarrow{j}z\xrightarrow{a}g(d)$ of $\alpha$ with $j$ inert and $a$ active. The active-lift clause of the approximation gives a $g$-cartesian edge $b:d_0\to d$ with $g(d_0)=z$ and $g(b)=a$. Thus $(b,j)$, retaining the chosen triangle, is a vertex $t$ of $F_g(d,\alpha)$ as defined in the cited weak-approximation node. No assumption on the colour fibre has been used here.

source.place: Definition 2.3.3.6 and proof of Lemma 2.3.3.10, printed pp. 260-261

proof.text: We prove that $t$ is terminal, including all coherence data. A vertex $s$ of $F_g(d,\alpha)$ consists of $\beta:d'\to d$, an inert $\gamma:x\to g(d')$, and a triangle $g(\beta)\gamma\simeq\alpha$. Together with $a j\simeq\alpha$ these specify a coherent square whose left edge is $\gamma$, right edge is $a:z\to g(d)$, top edge is $j$ and bottom edge is $g(\beta)$. The orthogonality comparison of [lem-coef-symmetric-inert-active-orthogonality] makes its space of fillers $h:g(d')\to z$, with $h\gamma\simeq j$ and $a h\simeq g(\beta)$ compatibly, contractible. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $g^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $b^{\mathrm{op}}$; opposites interchange the cartesian and cocartesian horn conditions in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Using the opposite mapping-space identification of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], this gives the homotopy pullback square with top row $\operatorname{Map}_D(d',d_0)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(d',d)$ and bottom row $\operatorname{Map}_P(g(d'),z)\to\operatorname{Map}_P(g(d'),g(d))$. Its homotopy fibre at $(\beta,h,a h\simeq g(\beta))$ is contractible. A point in that fibre is exactly a lift $k:d'\to d_0$, a triangle $b k\simeq\beta$ and its compatibility with $g(k)\simeq h$. Imposing $h\gamma\simeq j$ retains exactly the triangles defining a morphism $s\to t$ in the coherent factorization category. Hence its mapping space is equivalent to the contractible filler space above. This proves $\operatorname{Map}_{F_g(d,\alpha)}(s,t)\simeq *$ for every $s$, rather than merely existence of a morphism.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 2.3.3.10 and Proposition 2.1.2.4; cartesian mapping comparison: HTT Proposition 2.4.4.3, dual of the cited DAG criterion

proof.text: First check the quasicategory hypothesis for the contraction. The slice $D_{/d}$ is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For $B=P_{/g(d)}$, [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] with $K_0=\varnothing$ and $K=\Delta^0$ makes $B_{\alpha/}\to B$ a left fibration. Its pullback to $D_{/d}$ is a left fibration (a lift is obtained coordinatewise with the prescribed base). A left fibration over a quasicategory has a quasicategory total space by filling its base inner horn first; a full subcategory is a quasicategory since every filler has the same vertices. Hence $F_g(d,\alpha)$ is a quasicategory. By [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone], terminality supplies a simplicial map $F_g(d,\alpha)^{\triangleright}\to F_g(d,\alpha)$ restricting to the identity on the base and taking the cone vertex to $t$. Its realization contracts the realization of $F_g(d,\alpha)$: on each simplex use the linear cone coordinates $((1-u)v_0,\ldots,(1-u)v_r,u)$, $0\leq u\leq1$, and then the displayed simplicial map. These formulas agree on faces and degeneracies. Thus $F_g(d,\alpha)$ is weakly contractible. Since $d,\alpha$ were arbitrary and the projection-lift condition was already given, $g$ satisfies both weak-approximation conditions, and the original factorization $f=ge$ witnesses that $f$ is a weak approximation. This uses the arbitrary-functor clause of [lem-coef-symmetric-weak-approximation-algebras] directly; no passage of the colour hypothesis to a different strict fibre is necessary.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.3.10 and the arbitrary-functor clause of Definition 2.3.3.6

proof.text: Let $Q\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be any small symmetric infinity operad. Apply [lem-coef-symmetric-weak-approximation-algebras] to the original $f$, now known to be a weak approximation, and to the given equivalence of its original strict unary fibre. It gives an equivalence $f^*:\operatorname{Alg}(P,Q)\to\mathcal A_f(C,Q)$ of the full coherent algebra categories defined there by local colour projections and transport along $e$. This is part (1) of the source theorem and requires neither Kan colour categories nor $f$ itself to be a categorical fibration. We must still compare this category to the full subcategory $\mathcal B_f(C,Q)$ of relative functors carrying every $f$-inert edge to an inert edge of $Q$, because the marked mapping object tests all such edges. The source theorem alone does not define these two categories to be equal.

We show $\mathcal B_f(C,Q)\subseteq\mathcal A_f(C,Q)$, then compare essential images. Given $H\in\mathcal B_f(C,Q)$, the ambient relative functor equivalence in [lem-coef-symmetric-weak-approximation-algebras] supplies $K:D\to Q$ over the base and a natural equivalence $Ke\simeq H$ over the base. Let $u:d\to d_i$ be any local colour-projection lift for $g$; its image $g(u)$ is inert. A coherent quasi-inverse $v$ of the categorical equivalence $e$ gives an edge $u'=v(u)$ of $C$ and an equivalence of arrows $e(u')\simeq u$ in $D$, with equivalence components. Consequently $f(u')=ge(u')$ is equivalent, as an arrow of $P$, to the inert edge $g(u)$, so it is inert. Here inertness is invariant under equivalence of arrows: the base arrow is changed only by pointed-set isomorphisms, preserving the one-preimage condition; the cocartesian mapping-space square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] remains a homotopy pullback after pre- and postcomposition with equivalences. Thus $H(u')$ is inert. The equivalences $Ke\simeq H$ and $e(u')\simeq u$ show that $K(u)$ is equivalent to $H(u')$, hence inert by the same criterion. Their components are equivalences by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences]. Therefore $K\in\mathcal A_g(D,Q)$ and $H\in\mathcal A_f(C,Q)$. All subcategories here are full and replete; repleteness of $\mathcal B_f$ follows from the same invariance of inertness. Every restricted operad map $P\to Q$ belongs to $\mathcal B_f$, by the definition of an $f$-inert edge. Since Step 4 is fully faithful and essentially surjective onto $\mathcal A_f$, it is consequently fully faithful and essentially surjective onto $\mathcal B_f$ as well. More explicitly a quasi-inverse for Step 4 restricts to $\mathcal B_f$, since its return composite lies in the restricted-operad-map image; its two natural equivalences still lie in the full subcategories. This gives the required equivalence $\operatorname{Alg}(P,Q)\simeq\mathcal B_f(C,Q)$ with restriction as its forward functor.

source.place: Definition 2.3.3.20 and Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), followed by the explicit comparison with the all-inert marking of Definition 2.3.3.25; comparison written by the worker

proof.text: Identify this with the actual mapping test in $\mathsf M$. For $A=P^{\mathrm{in}}$ or $C^{\mathrm{in}/P}$, the underlying $r$-simplices of $\mathcal H_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}(A,Q^{\mathrm{in}})$ of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] are maps $A\times(\Delta^r)^\flat\to Q^{\mathrm{in}}$ over the base. By the product marking of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], preservation of markings requires exactly that the restriction at each vertex of $\Delta^r$ preserve the marked edges of $A$. Thus its underlying simplicial set is respectively $\operatorname{Alg}(P,Q)$ or $\mathcal B_f(C,Q)$, defined as the full subcategory on those vertices in Step 5. The enriched model axiom makes this Hom fibrant in the marked categorical model: take the cofibration $\varnothing\to A$ and the fibration $Q^{\mathrm{in}}\to *$. The first exists since cofibrations are monomorphisms and the second exists by the fibrancy assertion of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]. Consequently the Hom marks precisely its equivalences. For every $r$ the enriched adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A\times(\Delta^r)^\sharp,Q^{\mathrm{in}})$ with $\operatorname{Hom}((\Delta^r)^\sharp,\mathcal H(A,Q^{\mathrm{in}}))$. Since the latter Hom is marked by precisely its equivalences, these are exactly its core simplices. We obtain natural identities $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}(A,Q^{\mathrm{in}})=\operatorname{Alg}_A(Q)^\simeq$, where $\operatorname{Alg}_A(Q)$ denotes the corresponding category above. These identifications take restriction along the marked $f$ to the core of the very restriction functor of Step 5, degree by degree.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.6(W), Definition 2.3.3.20 and Definition 2.3.3.25; marked enrichment as in Appendix B.2

proof.text: The coherent quasi-inverse and the two natural equivalences of Step 5 restrict to the cores: functors carry inverse-and-two-triangle witnesses to such witnesses, and natural equivalences have equivalence components by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences]. Restricting the quasi-inverse and the two natural equivalences gives inverse maps on cores up to simplicial homotopies modeled on $\Delta^1$. Realizing those homotopies simplexwise, using the standard prism triangulation of $|\Delta^r|\times[0,1]$, gives homotopy inverse continuous maps, hence a bijection on components and inverse maps on all based homotopy groups (with the component path for basepoint change). Thus the core restriction in Step 6, which is $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}(P^{\mathrm{in}},Q^{\mathrm{in}})\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}(C^{\mathrm{in}/P},Q^{\mathrm{in}})$, is a weak homotopy equivalence for every small symmetric infinity operad $Q$. Now let $Z$ be any fibrant object of $\mathsf M$; by [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] these are exactly the $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}$-fibered objects. By [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibrant-objects], $Z=Q^{\mathrm{in}}$ for a small symmetric infinity operad $Q$ (its underlying map to $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$), with marking exactly the inert edges, including the zero-arity conditions. So $Z$ is one of the targets tested in Steps 4-6. Therefore the weak-equivalence test of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] applies to every fibrant target and shows that $f:C^{\mathrm{in}/P}\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$ is a weak equivalence. This reasoning proves the assertion for the original arbitrary coherent approximation $f$ throughout; there is no assertion that $f:C\to P$ is a categorical equivalence of total quasicategories.
